[[Kenny Florian]]|episodes=20|third_place=TBD|fourth_place=TBD}}''Not to be confused with the [[BattleBots Pro Championship 2009|BattleBots Pro Championship 2009 event]].'' {{Quote|Welcome to the next evolution in competitive robot combat – an all-new elite league that brings together the top 24 robots from around the world for an unprecedented season of destruction.|The ''Pro League'' as described by the ''BattleBots'' website}} The '''BattleBots Pro League''' is the name given to the upcoming season of ''[[BattleBots]]'' due to premiere on [[YouTube]] in July 2026. It is the first large-scale ''BattleBots'' event to take place since the show was dropped by [[Discovery]] following [[World Championship VII]] and [[BattleBots: Champions II|''BattleBots: Champions II'']]. [[File:Pro_League_2026_Header.jpg|A banner featuring Skorpios to promote the ''Pro League''.|thumb|left]] Featuring a total of 24 competitors, each of which were announced in a February 26, 2026 video uploaded to the ''BattleBots'' YouTube channel, the 2026 ''Pro League'' saw the return of several teams which had not made a competitive appearance since 2022, including [[End Game]], [[Ribbot]], [[DeathRoll]] and [[HUGE]], as well as some of the new breed which had since debuted at ''[[BattleBots Proving Ground|Proving Ground]]'' and ''[[BattleBots FaceOffs|FaceOffs]]'' such as [[Manta]] and [[Orbitron]]. Following their success at the Abu Dhabi ''Games of the Future'' event in December 2025, India's [[PY Roboticsz]] and [[Golden Fury]] also made their first ''BattleBots'' showing. Notably absent from the 2026 ''Pro League'' are reigning Giant Nut winner [[SawBlaze]] as well as stalwart competitors such as [[Lock-Jaw]], [[Whiplash]] and [[Hydra]]. Due to the considerably smaller field of robots compared to the 50-bot roster for World Championship VII, applicants such as [[Banshee]] and fan favorite [[Traves T.]] were not accepted as full competitors despite showing interest and competing at both ''Proving Ground'' and ''FaceOffs''. [[Reserves|Alternates]] were selected to protect against dropouts, and these were confirmed to be [[Team Horizon]] and [[Calypso]], [[Wildcat Robotics]] and [[Disarray]], [[Team Small Robots]] and [[Banshee]] as well as newcomers [[Nemesis (2026)|Nemesis]]. The ''Pro League'' signals a return to ''BattleBots'' in a full-time capacity for presenters [[Chris Rose]], [[Kenny Florian]], ring announcer [[Faruq Tauheed]] and Match Steward [[Mike Jeffries]]. Also returning is former competitor [[Fon Davis]], joined on the judging panel by [[Pete Abrahamson]] and, for the first time, [[Bil Dwyer]]. For the third week of filming, however, [[Xyla Foxlin]] filled in for Dwyer.https://www.instagram.com/p/DX2eXhiEouU/ With [[John Remar]] stepping aside from refereeing to work full-time in the show's production, [[David Sanfilippo]] became head referee and was joined by [[Alex Watson]]. Despite the confirmed involvement of international competitors hailing from Canada, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand and India, the event is not being marketed as a 'World Championship', likely due to being untelevised. BattleBots_Pro_League_Group_F.jpg|Group F. == Format == [[File:BattleBots Pro League logo 2026.png|thumb|left|The event's logo.|162x162px]]A group stage format akin to [[BattleBots FaceOffs|''BattleBots FaceOffs'']] was chosen in place of the [[Fight Night]] format which had taken place in every large-scale ''BattleBots'' competition since [[World Championship III]]. This sees six groups of four competitors fight three fights each, with the best-performing robots winning their group and advancing to the single-elimination tournament. In the event of equal win-loss record, the amount of knockouts and then knockout time are the next deciding factors. Groups A-C make up the first weekend of filming, taking place across April 18-19, 2026. Following this are Groups D-F, which take place on April 25 and April 26.https://battlebots.com/proleague/#tickets These six groups were revealed on April 7, 2026.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QeLlbSrz5PI Who Can Tame This Beast? – Unveiled: Group A in the BATTLEBOTS PRO LEAGUE powered by BRIGHT DATA] After all six groups have finished, the group winners will proceed to the knockout stage of the competition, which takes place with filming spanning May 2 and May 3. The ''BattleBots'' websites states there to be quarter-finals, semi-finals and a final, implying as many as eight robots would make the knockout tournament from the six groups. This was later stated by Will Bales in the Group E preview video.[https://youtu.be/LXYTwFYlXNs?si=o2lWtxbPVKz6hhzl&t=45 Revealed – The Group of Death. Group E of the BATTLEBOTS PRO LEAGUE powered by BRIGHT DATA] Across the weekend of May 2-3, there is also dedicated time for exhibition battles and demonstrations. The ''Pro League'' consists of 20 total episodes uploaded weekly to the ''BattleBots'' YouTube channel on Thursdays, beginning July 2. It is not currently known how long each episode will be, though [[Bot Bash Party Crew|Zach Lytle]] of [[Skorpios]] confirmed each episode to contain three battles and that the ''BattleBots'' website would unveil each episode's fights leading up to the knockout rounds on June 29.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WHFVF4eFa8c Battlebots Pro League News Just Dropped!] == Reveals and Trailers == A February 6, 2026 announcement revealed a "new era" for ''BattleBots'' as a partnership with Bright Data would allow for more content during the year, promising an update scheduled for February 26. The announcement came in the form of a four-minute YouTube video featuring Chris, Kenny and Faruq announcing the ''Pro League'' and each of the competitors one-by-one. [[File:Pro_League_2026_Trailer.mp4|right|link=Special:FilePath/Pro_League_2026_Trailer.mp4|thumb|300x300px]]Tickets were made available to the general public from March 2, though Facebook Supporters received pre-sale access from February 27. Though a formal announcement by ''BattleBots'' has not yet been made, an article from Yahoo Finance cites June 25 as the premiere.https://finance.yahoo.com/news/battlebots-powered-bright-data-greenlights-171500042.html In mid-June, several competitors including [[Team Malice]] and [[Team Copperhead]] stated on their social media pages that their appearances would air in July. The reason has not been explicitly stated, and the ''BattleBots'' website was later updated to reflect this. Later in the month, CoreWeave was announced as an official sponsor of the ''BattleBots Pro League'', and with this announcement, a new premiere date of July 2 was confirmed. The official 53-second trailer for Pro League was shared on June 25, confirming weekly episode uploads. Announced by Chris Rose, the trailer shows brief clips from various confirmed group stage battles, highlighting the "AI-controlled" [[Orbitron]] and featuring to-camera clips from builders [[Team Orbitron|Steven Szczeszynski]], [[Team HyperShock|Will Bales]], [[Team Terrortops|Ben Burton]] and [[Team Midnight Invention|Greg Needel]]. The trailer ends with [[Faruq Tauheed]] delivering a variation of his famous catchphrase, "It's Pro League fighting time!". Ahead of the series premiere, ''BattleBots'' opened applications for '''''Pro League'' 2027'''. == Rule Changes == === Kinetic Energy === Ahead of this tournament, an upper cap on kinetic energy was enforced for the first time, set at 150kJ. However, this is not known to have affected any competing teams. === Judging Criteria === The judging criteria was again adapted for the ''Pro League'', as briefly mentioned by Chris Rose in [[BattleBots Pro League/Episode 1|Episode 1]]. Fights were judged in just two categories, Damage and Engagement, with the latter being an amalgamation of Control and Aggression categories seen in past seasons. It has not yet been publicly explained how the two categories are weighted compared to the [https://battlebots.fandom.com/wiki/World_Championship_VII#Judges'_Decisions_and_Appeals 11-point system]. Other aspects of the judging criteria from the [https://battlebots.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Judges-Guide.2022.0.pdf 2022 Judges Guide] introduced for World Championship VII are presumed to be unchanged.{{Cit}} == Changes to the BattleBox == In the leadup to the ''BattleBots Pro League'', the logo of new sponsor Bright Data adorned areas of the BattleBox. Metalwork with Lexan walls bolted in place and a sloped top was constructed atop the drivers' booths in order to prevent the possibility of robots becoming stuck on this previously flat surface. Much of the existing arena Lexan was replaced and the arena floor was freshly painted. Within the drivers' booths, new tapout buttons were fitted to allow for fights to be determined by TKO. This was first seen in the first fight of [[BattleBots Pro League/Episode 2|Episode 2]] when [[JackPot|JackPot's]] [[Vegas Combat Robotics|team]] decided to end its fight with [[Copperhead]] by pushing their tapout button to declare a TKO. == Pro League Standings == ''NOTE: Standings accurate as of the most recent Pro League episode. In the event of robots being tied on win/loss record, points are allocated to robots and are weighted depending on the means in which a fight is won or lost. Knockout wins and unanimous judges' decisions count for more points than a win by split judges' decision, thought the points allocated to each eventiality is not publicly known.
